versions.statuteQuote: Such notices shall be provided to the tenant no less than 60 days prior to the end of the rental agreement term.
The landlord shall provide the tenant with this written notice of rent increase at least 90 days prior to the end of the rental agreement term.

summaryForModel: A landlord who owns more than four rental units in Virginia (or more than a 10% interest in more than four) must give written notice of a rent increase for a renewal term, and written notice of nonrenewal. Until July 1, 2027 both notices are due at least 60 days before the lease ends. From July 1, 2027 a rent increase notice is due at least 90 days before the lease ends and must give the tenant at least 30 days to decide whether to renew; nonrenewal notice stays at 60 days. This does not apply to a periodic tenancy under § 55.1-1253(C). A lease that allows shorter notice conflicts with this when the landlord is that size.
paraphraseExamples: Landlord may increase rent at renewal by giving 30 days' notice.
This Lease renews automatically; any new rent will be stated in a notice sent 15 days before the end of the term.
tenantExplanation: If your landlord owns more than four rentals, they have to tell you early if your rent is going up at renewal or if they won't renew: at least 60 days before your lease ends. From July 1, 2027, a rent increase needs at least 90 days' notice.
action: Ask your landlord how many units they own. If it is more than four, you can ask them to change the notice period to match Virginia law.
